summary: A vault owner's own settings: the profile record, how dates and numbers read, a change-password path both kinds share, a read-only main currency, dimension configuration, session listing and the idle lock, and self-service account deletion.

profilePayload.value: { mainCurrency required, createdAt required, idleLockMinutes optional, one of the offered periods, with absent meaning 15, locale optional BCP 47 with absent or unrecognized meaning the browser's and never validated against a list, dateStyle optional one of locale dmy ymd mdy, groupSeparator optional one of locale thin apostrophe comma period none, moneyPlaces optional string one of locale 0 2 with locale meaning two, dimensions optional with absent or empty meaning none }. Registration writes the two required keys and nothing else, and each optional key appears the first time the user sets it

profileSingleton.value: one profile record per vault, the only record guaranteed to exist after registration. The API enforces no singleton, and clients treat the highest version as authoritative

oneFormatter.value: every figure and date reaches the screen through one formatter built from the profile, answering money at moneyPlaces for a figure in any currency (the main currency, and a holding's own unit whose symbol-table kind is currency), quantity for a figure in any other unit, parseQuantity, rate at six places, date, and parseDate. Money rounds half-even. parseDate returns nothing rather than guessing: a two-digit year and an impossible date are refused. Defaults are read from Intl at run time, never tabulated. A groupSeparator equal to the locale's decimal point is not applied. No setting writes any record but the profile

dateWriters.value: date and parseDate serve a date field and nothing else. Dates shown for reading go through one writer per slot: longDate (day, abbreviated month, year: a sentence, a row, a tooltip, a table), fullDate (month in full, for a heading), dayMonth (day and month, long or abbreviated, for a label that implies the year), monthYear (month in full and year) and dateTime (a moment in the browser's time zone: longDate, a comma, hours and minutes in the locale's form). Under dateStyle locale they spell the month in the locale's language. Under dmy, ymd or mdy every writer but monthYear writes the whole date in that style, the text date writes, and dayMonth writes the year too. monthYear keeps its spelling under every style

dateWriterExamples.value: en-US, no dateStyle, 2026-09-20: date 09/20/2026, longDate Sep 20, 2026, fullDate September 20, 2026, dayMonth September 20 and Sep 20, monthYear September 2026, dateTime starting Sep 20, 2026, . en-US, dateStyle dmy: date, longDate, fullDate and both dayMonth forms 20.09.2026, dateTime starting 20.09.2026, , monthYear September 2026. The settings sample line writes its date with longDate

quantityFormat.value: a stored value in any unit that is not a currency (a metal or free text) is shown digit for digit from its decimal string: never rounded, never padded, the group mark in force between groups of three in the integer part and the configured decimal point. "12.125" reads 12.125, "12.50" reads 12.50 and "80" reads 80. It does not follow moneyPlaces. It formats a stored string and nothing computed. A negative value is signed as money is. The same rule holds as text and in a field, on every screen

parseQuantity.value: the reverse of quantity, for a field. The configured decimal point is the point, and so is . wherever . is not the group mark in force. The group mark in force is accepted only between groups of three digits in the integer part, and anywhere else the input is malformed, never dropped, because 12.5 read as 125 under a period group mark is a silent tenfold error. Returns the canonical decimal string or nothing

canonicalDecimalString.value: -?(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(\.[0-9]{1,12})?, a zero carrying no sign. Defined by record-snapshot.md and returned by parseQuantity

editPrefill.value: a field that edits a stored figure prefills it through quantity, whatever the unit, money included, because a prefill at moneyPlaces saved untouched would write the rounding. A field whose text still equals its prefill is untouched and is never parsed, so it saves the stored string itself

changePasswordEndpoint.value: POST /api/auth/change-password { currentAuthKey, salt, kdf, authKey, wrappedDek, dekNonce }. The server verifies currentAuthKey against the stored hash, then replaces the password credential row's params and verifier and, for a vault owner, that credential's one dek_wrappers row, in one transaction. No other row is written

changePasswordComparesEpoch.value: for a vault owner the transaction compares the vault epoch after BEGIN IMMEDIATE and before any write, because a page holding a DEK an import replaced would otherwise wrap the old key under the new password and leave every record unreadable. A replaced epoch answers Conflict {"refused":"vault-replaced"} with a correct currentAuthKey, and credentials, dek_wrappers and sessions stay as they were, so the restored vault still opens with the unchanged password. An administrator has no epoch and the header on their request is ignored

deleteAccountComparesEpoch.value: DELETE /api/auth/account compares the vault epoch after BEGIN IMMEDIATE, so a page that confirmed deleting a vault since replaced deletes nothing. A replaced epoch with a correct authKey and confirmUsername answers Conflict {"refused":"vault-replaced"} and deletes nothing

deleteAccountDeletesTheEpoch.value: account deletion removes the principal row, every credential row, every wrapper, every record, the vault epoch and every session in one transaction. It leaves no vault_epochs row for the account

importEndsNoSession.value: an import ends no session. A password change alone ends every other session and keeps the current one, and log out everywhere ends every session including the current one

changePasswordDerivesAtCurrentParameters.value: the client derives the new keys with the server's current default KDF parameters read from the envelope the app shell embeds, not the old ones. A password change is also a KDF upgrade

changePasswordBar.value: at least 12 characters and zxcvbn at least 3, the same bar as registration

changePasswordByKind.value: the server discriminates on the session's principal kind and not on which fields arrived, so a vault owner's request without a wrapper is a Bad Request and an administrator's with one is too. An administrator sends no wrapper and their current password is verified server-side only, because the second check was the unwrap and there is nothing to unwrap

changePasswordSessions.value: invalidates all other sessions for the account and keeps the current one. The client keeps its in-memory DEK and no re-login is needed

noRemovePassword.value: there is no remove-password action and there will not be one. Changing the password replaces the row, and nothing deletes it short of deleting the account

exportWarning.value: the screen must warn that existing export files still open with the old password, since they carry their own salt and wrapped DEK

mainCurrencyIsReadOnly.value: displayed, not editable in v1, with a one-line note that it is fixed at registration and why. Import is the one exception, and it is not a loophole, because it replaces the price history along with the profile

dimensionsShape.value: a list of { id, label, archivedAt, values: [{ id, label, archivedAt }] }

dimensionIdFormat.value: 8 characters of [a-z0-9] from crypto.getRandomValues, minted at creation, checked for uniqueness against the profile already in memory. Each character is drawn uniformly from the 36 by rejection: a random value outside the range is redrawn, never reduced modulo 36. Opaque and immutable, never shown, never typed, never derived from the label

dimensionOrder.value: order in values is the band order in the stacked chart, and order of dimensions is the order of the dashboard's Group by select. Reordering writes one record

deletingIsArchiving.value: deleting a dimension or a single value sets archivedAt and keeps the definition in the profile, leaving every account's dims entry untouched. There is no remove-everywhere option and no multi-record write anywhere in this feature

flagShape.value: a dimension with a single value is the shape that replaces a yes/no tag, and the account form renders it as a checkbox rather than a select. Absence of an entry means no

valuesBeyondFour.value: values may exceed four and the chart folds the remainder into Other. The screen says so rather than capping the list, because the limit is a rendering constraint and not a data one

deleteAccountEndpoint.value: DELETE /api/auth/account { authKey, confirmUsername }. The server checks authKey against the stored hash in constant time and that confirmUsername equals the session user's normalized username. A mismatch on either is a Bad Request and deletes nothing. It deletes the principal row, every credential row, every wrapper, every record, the vault epoch and every session in one transaction, with nothing soft-deleted

deleteAccountHasNoAdministratorGuard.value: no last-administrator check, because a vault owner is never an administrator. The dialog offers export first as the primary action and deletion as the secondary one

idleLock.value: user-configurable, default 15, stored as idleLockMinutes in the encrypted profile record, so it follows the user across devices and the server never sees it. Absent means 15. No setting disables it. There is no idle rule for an administrator. A changed period applies at once, not from the next activity

idleLockOfferedPeriods.value: 5, 10, 15, 30, 45 and 60 minutes, with 15 selected on a vault that has never set it

idleLockStoredValueRule.value: any other stored number, a fraction included, locks at the nearest offered period and the shorter on a tie, and the select shows that period. A stored value that is not a number means 15. Stored 0, 500, 7 and 7.5 lock at 5, 60, 5 and 5

sessionExpiry.value: absolute, 12 hours from issue, for both kinds. login.md, Rules owns the value

sessionEndpoints.value: POST /api/auth/logout invalidates the current session, with the client discarding its in-memory keys first, and answers OK without a session. POST /api/auth/logout-all invalidates every session for the user including the current one, and there is no all-except-this-one variant. GET /api/sessions returns [{ id, issuedAt, lastActiveAt, current }], where id is an opaque handle and never the cookie's value

sessionsListOnlyLive.value: GET /api/sessions lists only live sessions, meaning not past the absolute expiry. An expired row is left off whether or not a sign-in has deleted it yet. It returns only the session user's own sessions

unlockAddsNoSession.value: unlocking signs in on the same server session and adds no row. Locking and unlocking leaves GET /api/sessions with the same entries, the same id and the same issuedAt. This screen owns only the idle period

noSessionMetadata.value: no IP address and no user-agent is stored in a session row, and no endpoint returns any, because none is recorded. The one trace of a connection is the attempts table's keyed address key from a failed sign-in, which GET /api/sessions never returns and which cannot be read back without SECRET_KEY (spec/architecture.md#storage-data-handling)

openSessionsNotice.value: Solvent keeps no IP address readable and records no devices.

wrongCurrentAuthKeyOrConfirmUsername.condition: checked server-side, since a client bypassing the dialog is the case that matters (spec/features/account-settings.md#delete-my-account)

vaultReplaced.condition: a vault owner's change-password or account-deletion request carrying the epoch from before an import. The body is {"refused":"vault-replaced"} and nothing is written (spec/features/account-settings.md#acceptance-criteria)

changePasswordWrapperMismatch.condition: an administrator session carrying a wrapper, or a vault owner session without one (spec/features/account-settings.md#change-password)

fixtures: a vault holding records written before a password change, decrypted again afterwards in the same session and after a fresh login

locale de-DE and groupSeparator apostrophe with an m² holding stored as "1234.5", for the quantity display and the parseQuantity cases 1’234,50 and 12.5; locale de-DE and groupSeparator period for the cases 1.234,5 and 12.5 (the last refused)

focus: the change-password transaction must be shown to write nothing but the password credential row and its own wrapper, with every record's ciphertext byte-identical afterwards. Counting requests is not the same as comparing rows, and a re-encryption of records would pass every functional test while costing exactly what the DEK indirection exists to save

a change-password carrying the pre-import epoch with a correct currentAuthKey must answer vault-replaced and leave credentials, dek_wrappers and sessions as they were, and the restored vault must still open with the unchanged password. A server that skips the epoch wraps the old DEK under the new password and every record becomes unreadable, which only a restore-then-change sequence shows

the account deletion carrying the pre-import epoch must delete nothing with a correct authKey and confirmUsername, so a page that confirmed deleting a vault since replaced cannot destroy it, and a deletion that goes through must leave no vault_epochs row. Asserting the wrong-authKey refusal alone passes a deletion that never compares the epoch
a wrong currentAuthKey must be rejected server-side even with the client-side unwrap bypassed. The client check is the one an attacker skips, so the test has to call the endpoint directly

DELETE /api/auth/account must be called directly with a wrong authKey and with a mismatched confirmUsername. The typed username is a deliberate second factor of intent, and treating it as a UI formality passes every dialog-driven test

'no operation in the dimensions feature writes more than one record' must be asserted by counting PUT requests across create, rename, reorder, archive and restore, and by comparing every account record byte for byte. A multi-record write that happens to succeed is invisible otherwise
archiving a dimension and restoring it must return every account to its band with no account record written in either direction, which is the assertion that catches a tidy-up write

GET /api/sessions must be asserted against the endpoint's full response shape, so the test fails if an IP address or user-agent field is added later. Asserting the absence of a value is not the same as asserting the absence of a field

lock and unlock must be shown to leave GET /api/sessions with the same entries, the same id and the same issuedAt, compared before and after. An unlock that inserts a row or moves issuedAt looks identical from the screen
an expired row not yet deleted must be absent from GET /api/sessions, asserted with the row still in the table. A listing that relies on a sign-in's cleanup passes every test that signs in first

the password change must keep the initiating session alive while killing every other one, asserted from both sides, because an implementation that kills all of them still passes the half of the criterion people write
the idle-lock setting must be shown to appear in plaintext nowhere in the database, which means scanning the stored rows rather than trusting that it went into the profile payload

the stored idle periods 0, 500, 7 and 7.5 must each be asserted by the period the lock fires at and by the value the select shows, with a changed period locking at the new one with no activity after the change. A select-only test passes an implementation that locks at the raw stored number, and 7.5 is the tie that shows the shorter side wins

each date writer must be asserted on a screen that shows a date, not on the formatter alone, under dateStyle locale and under dmy, with monthYear unchanged by the style. A screen that spells a month with date, or that writes digits with longDate, passes the formatter test
the formatter must be asserted on every screen that shows a figure, not on the formatter alone. A screen that formats a number itself passes every formatter test while ignoring the setting

the USD and XAU-ozt holdings must each be asserted in both places their figure appears, with its unit and in the holding page's list of values. A formatter keyed on the main currency alone, or on moneyPlaces for every unit, passes the main-currency cases while rounding 12.125 ounces to 12 or padding 80 m² to 80.00

quantity display must be asserted with values that rounding or padding would change, "12.125", "12.50" and "80", under moneyPlaces 0 and under 2. A value like "12.5" or "3.00" passes a formatter that pads to two places

parseQuantity must be asserted on the refusal as well as the reading: 12.5 under a period group mark is refused, never read as 125. A parser that drops a misplaced group mark passes every accepted-input case

the edit prefill must be shown by saving the dialog untouched and comparing the stored value string byte for byte. A dialog that prefills 1’000 for "1000.40" and parses it back on save looks identical until the record is read
